- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c3c7bfcbd8b824f84a18dea317de1e1ef1a5dbef`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-jobs.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.job-pull.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.compose-stacks-job-name-across-packages-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/stack-compose-duplicate-entry-census.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack-composed-job-name-across-holders.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack-residual-extension-jobs.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + none in the diff beyond these; read in the cited code and not reviewed: packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts (`mergeCollection`, `resolveArtifactCollections`), packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts (`collectBundleJobs`)
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

Faces: published schema (`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`, the semantic migration entry) and narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset). Inputs: card #36431 with all five comments, the PR body, file list and four comments, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head (58 success, 11 skipped, none failed or pending).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set narrowing, cross-holder (right).** `composeStacks` now refuses one job name ENABLED in two holders of a result that carries `packages[]`: two package bodies, or a body and the residual. The code is `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID`, 422, through the existing artifact pass. This is the route the claim took under 元判据 ②: the install door and the binder already refuse, so composition refuses. The card's to-do 1 (where the clash is judged) is answered at composition, and the binder stays as the backstop.
- **Reading of the residual (right).** `composedJobDeclarations` files a body's jobs under the body and the residual's by count beyond the bodies' copies, matching by object identity first. That is the count `jobNameCollisions` makes (`boundCount - declaredCount`), and it agrees with `preservePackageEntries` on which input becomes a body (`stack.manifest`, or the carried `packages[]`).
- **Enabled only (right).** `enabled === false` is skipped, the same test the binder makes. A disabled twin composes.
- **Accept-set narrowing the changeset does not state (right, see N1).** The residual's own door now takes its jobs from the same reading. On `main` a residual job whose name a body also carried was claimed as that body's copy and never read. Two residual jobs of one name beside a body job of that name therefore composed on `main`, and are now the one-package finding, which counts a disabled job too. That is ruling A (#35228: one package, every door) applied to entries the by-name claim hid. It is a wider refusal than the binder's for the disabled case, which is the one-package door's existing reading.
- **Unchanged (right).** A flat composition has one holder and keeps the one-package finding. A body's flattened copy is not a second job. Distinct names compose.
- **Identity dedupe across holders (wrong, see S1).** One job object reached through two holders is counted once, and the binder counts it twice.
- **Public surface.** No export added or changed: the three new symbols are module-private, and `check:generated` is reported up to date. The runtime change is two docblocks on symbols `src/index.ts` does not export.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec`: `minor`, marked BREAKING, with a FROM → TO line and the `adr-0087: registered compose-stacks-job-name-across-packages-refused` marker; the entry file is in the diff. That matches what the diff publishes: an accept-set narrowing of `composeStacks` and no new export. `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head. `@objectstack/runtime` (comment text only) and `@objectstack/cloud-connection` (one test file) ship no changed byte, so no entry is owed for either.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — on the PR body and on the changeset, and correct: the diff takes an accepted input away and adds no capability.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the os-dev-report. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 3 locally (prerequisite not met): answered by CI. `Build Core`, `Type Check · consumer gates` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are `success` on this head.
- Dev flag, out-of-scope finding (`resolveArtifactCollections` claims a body's job by name, so a top-level residual job shadows a body job with no copy and the body's job is never scheduled): confirmed by reading `mergeCollection` and `claimedIdentities` in `packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts`. It is outside this diff and reachable only by an artifact no composition built. It goes to the seat to file or set aside; it does not block this PR.
- Stale reason text in the shipped entry `stack-residual-extension-registered-and-jobs-judged`: left as shipped, superseded by the new entry. Accepted.
- SQL push-down: no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join in this diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**S1 (should-fix) — one job OBJECT reached through two holders composes, and the boot schedules neither.** Read from code, not driven.

- `composedJobDeclarations` keeps one `seen` set across every input and holder (`declare` returns early on an object it has already filed). Its docblock says so: "One entry OBJECT reached through two inputs is one declaration, counted once".
- The binder does not count that way. `collectBundleJobs` reads `resolveArtifactCollections(bundle).jobs`; `mergeCollection` appends every body's jobs the top level does not claim, with no dedupe between bodies; `jobNameCollisions` counts entries by name. Two bodies holding the same job give the binder two enabled jobs of the name, and it refuses both.
- The shape is reachable through strict `defineStack`, because a flat `composeStacks` concatenates by reference (`arrays.flat()`): `const base = defineStack({ jobs: [J] })`, `a = composeStacks([base, defineStack({ manifest: sales, … })])`, `b = composeStacks([base, defineStack({ manifest: billing })])`, then `composeStacks([a, b], { manifest: 'preserve' })`. Both assembled bodies carry `J`. The second declaration is dropped, the name has one holder, and the artifact composes. It is the "shared base inside two nested compositions" the docblock itself names.
- The same holds for a body and the residual (`composeStacks([a, base], { manifest: 'preserve' })`), and inside one holder (`composeStacks([m, sub, sub])` with a job in `sub`, top level `[J, J]`). The one-holder case composed on `main` too; the jobs reading is rewritten here and keeps it.
- Sentences this makes false on this head:
  - the card's acceptance, "Two jobs of one name never compose into a boot that silently schedules neither";
  - `app-artifact-handlers.ts`, "so an artifact it built never reaches this refusal";
  - the changeset, "Read as the binder reads it";
  - the entry's `acceptanceCriteria`, that a stack which loads without the finding boots with no `NOT SCHEDULED` error.
- Precedent: #35228 review S3 settled the same question for `hooks`. A hook reached twice is counted twice, because a built artifact binds each copy (`stack-object-extension-duplicate-target.test.ts`, "a hook reached twice is refused"). Jobs are bound per copy as well.
- Fix direction: count a job per place it is reached, as `hooks` are. The copy matching inside a nested input does not depend on `seen` (it uses `bodyJobs` and the count). Pin the shared-object pair across two bodies, across a body and the residual, and inside one holder.
- Not a regression: each of these shapes composed on `main`. It is graded should-fix because the refusal is right wherever it fires and the shape needs one built stack reached through two inputs.

**N1 (nit) — the changeset's "as before" is not exact.** "Two residual jobs of one name stay the one-package finding … as before" holds only when no body carries the name. Beside a body job of that name the pair composed on `main` (the by-name claim) and is refused now, a disabled pair included. The changeset and the entry's `surface` could say so. Prose only.

Files, each against the code it cites:

- `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`: holds, apart from S1.
  - Body or residual per input agrees with `preservePackageEntries` and with the concat pass (a carried `packages[]` wins over `manifest`; an empty carried array yields no body).
  - The nested branch matches by identity, then by count, so an in-memory copy and a JSON-reloaded copy are both read as copies; the JSON case names the later entry as the residual's, which the docblock states.
  - `collectComposedJobNameErrors` skips a name with fewer than two holders, so each one-holder pair stays its own door's finding and is not reported twice.
  - The replaced "Known gap" docblock and the four cross-references agree with the code.
- `18.compose-stacks-job-name-across-packages-refused.ts`: `surface`, `replacement` and `reason` match the code and the changeset. No D2 conversion is right, since which job to keep is the author's call. `acceptanceCriteria` is subject to S1.
- `packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts`: comment text only. The backstop paragraph is accurate except the one sentence S1 names.
- `stack-composed-job-name-across-holders.test.ts`: 17 cases. Every refusal asserts code, status and one issue; the nested cases carry anti-vacuity checks. It has no case for one job object reached through two holders (S1).
- `stack-compose-duplicate-entry-census.test.ts`, `stack-residual-extension-jobs.test.ts`: the two CONTROLs pinned the behaviour this card changes. Dropping the `jobs` row and giving each body its own job name are right, and the new file pins the refusal.
- `app-artifact-handlers.job-pull.test.ts`, `marketplace-install-local-jobs.test.ts`: the fixtures now hand-build the backstop artifact through stand-in names restored after JSON. Every binder and install-door assertion is kept, and `handBuilt` is pinned equal to a real composition on two layouts that still compose.
